description: Helium is a colorless, odorless, non-toxic, inert, monatomic gas and the first in the noble gas group in the periodic table. It has symbol He and atomic number 2. It is the second-lightest and second-most abundant element in the observable universe, after hydrogen.
uses: Liquid helium is used in cryogenics and in the cooling of superconducting magnets, with its main commercial application in MRI scanners. Other industrial uses include as a pressurizing and purge gas, as a protective atmosphere for arc welding, and in crystal growing processes. It is also used as a lifting gas in balloons and airships, and is important in scientific research for studying quantum mechanics and phenomena near absolute zero.
characteristics: Helium has the lowest boiling point among all elements and does not have a melting point at standard pressures. It is colorless and odorless, and helium-4 exhibits superfluidity at temperatures near absolute zero. Terrestrial helium is relatively rare at 5.2 ppm by volume in the atmosphere, but can be concentrated in natural gas fields in concentrations as great as 7% by volume.
